patch.objective: Recognize red flags that need emergency referral: chest pain, stroke symptoms, sepsis, an acute abdomen, ectopic pregnancy and suicidal intent
secondaryObjectives: Build and prioritize a differential diagnosis from history, examination and test results, ruling out the dangerous causes first

sources.cite: ANCC, Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP-BC) test content outline (effective 2026-10-30): Diagnosis
sources.note: Relayed from the course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/fnp.ts), which read the outline 2026-11-14, not re-read for this band. Diagnosis is 17% of the exam.

sources.note: The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

sources.cite: 2025 AHA/ACC et al. Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (AHA 'Top things to know')
sources.note: Relayed from the FNP (clinical practice) case clinic-severe-bp-stroke-signs, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the course seed, which read the AHA page 2026-11-14 (and the PCCN seed re-read it the same day). Severe hypertension above 180/120 WITHOUT acute target-organ damage is evaluated and treated as an outpatient with oral drugs; WITH acute target-organ damage it is a hypertensive emergency treated in hospital.

sources.cite: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (AHA 'Top things to know')
sources.note: Relayed from the FNP (clinical practice) case clinic-severe-bp-stroke-signs, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the PCCN and CEN course seeds, which read the AHA page 2026-11-14. IV thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of onset (selected patients later with advanced imaging), so the time last known well decides treatment; blood pressure below 185/110 before thrombolysis is a hospital step.

Relayed from the FNP (clinical practice) case clinic-severe-bp-stroke-signs, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the course seed (read 2026-11-07). Level 1 hypoglycemia below 70 mg/dL; used here only because low glucose can mimic a stroke, so a fingerstick is part of the check.
